evidence: mobile-native/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/realtor/PortalListingsRepository.kt:111-154 — getPortfolioAnalytics() builds the realtor dashboard by calling listMyListings(limit = 100) (line 113) and then aggregating ONLY over the returned `listings` collection. The server clamps limit to 1..=100 (documented on listMyListings line 42), so a realtor who owns more than 100 listings silently gets a portfolio that covers only the first 100.

The truncation is invisible: MyListingsResponse carries `val total: Long` (PortalListingModels.kt:47) which is the true owned-listing count, but getPortfolioAnalytics never reads `.total` — it uses `.listings` (the capped page) for everything. Consequences on a >100-listing account: totalListings = listings.size (line 145) reports 100 instead of the real count; activeListings (line 146) undercounts; and every aggregate — totalViews/totalInquiries/totalFavorites and the viewsTrend/inquiriesTrend series (lines 126-152) — omits all listings past the first 100. The dashboard shows wrong, under-reported numbers with no error or indication.

There is also no offset paging loop: the function issues exactly one listMyListings call at offset 0. Fix: page through with the existing `offset` param until collected.size >= response.total (or loop while a full page of 100 is returned), then aggregate over the complete set; and set totalListings from response.total rather than listings.size so the count is correct even if per-listing analytics are skipped.

mobile-native/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/realtor/PortalListingsRepository.kt:119-124 — getPortfolioAnalytics() fans out one analytics HTTP request per listing with no concurrency limit: `listings.map { listing -> async { getListingAnalytics(listing.id).getOrNull() } }.awaitAll()`. With the current page size that launches up to 100 simultaneous GET /api/v1/my/listings/{id}/analytics calls from a mobile device.

On a large portfolio this bursts the shared HttpClientProvider connection pool, hammers the mobile radio, and is a natural trigger for server-side rate limiting (429) — and because per-listing failures are swallowed by getOrNull() (line 121), a rate-limited subset silently drops out of the aggregate, compounding the accuracy problem in the sibling finding. Consider bounding concurrency (e.g. chunk the listings and awaitAll per chunk, or gate with a Semaphore of ~4-8 permits) so the dashboard degrades gracefully instead of stampeding the backend.
